description.narrative: The Project is expected to increase access to equity capital and support value creation for agri-focused businesses in Pakistan, where agriculture accounts for 23 percent of GDP and 37 percent of employment but faces rising costs and high exposure to climate risks, including flooding, extreme heat, and water scarcity. Pakistan ranks 151st out of 187 countries on the ND-GAIN Index, with over 80 percent of the population exposed to high climate-related risk. At a market level, the Project is also expected to strengthen Pakistan's nascent private equity market, which comprises four funds with approximately US$80m in assets under management, only one of which remains active, and has seen no new fund launches since 2018. By attracting a new mix of commercial and institutional investors, ACAP is expected to demonstrate the commercial viability of equity investing in Pakistan and catalyze future market activity.

The proposed investment is a senior equity commitment of up to US$10m in Acumen Climate Action Pakistan Cooperatief U.A. (ACAP or the Fund). ACAP is Pakistans first climate-focused, agribusiness-oriented and closed-end private equity fund, targeting a total fund size of US$80m. The Fund is structured with (i) 66.25% senior equity, and (ii) a minimum of 33.75% junior equity. ACAP will target early-growth and growth-stage businesses with strong competitive positioning and high potential for market leadership across three priority verticals: (i) farmer platforms and financial solutions; (ii) smart farming; and (iii) post-harvest technologies. The Fund expects to make equity and equity-linked investments in 1215 portfolio companies, with individual ticket sizes ranging from US$1m to US$7.5m. ACAP intends to drive value creation and impact through (i) support for investees organic growth via the provision of patient capital,(ii) targeted operational improvements, and (iii) ecosystem improvements via sector insights and knowledge and stakeholder convenings, enabled by a dedicated, grant-funded technical assistance program of up to US$10m. The project is expected to be supported by the UK-IFC Pakistan Climate Adaptation and Innovation Investment Facility for Pakistan (CIFPAK) as described in the Blended Finance Section.
